deed: ישראל מקימה בית חולים שדה במערב אוקראינה ומטפלת בכ-6,000 חולים
title: Israel set up the "Kochav Meir" field hospital in western Ukraine and treated about 6,000 patients

trailer.text: According to Israel Hayom, the Israeli field hospital in Ukraine was a joint effort of Israel's Health and Foreign Ministries and of Sheba Medical Center, which operated it. According to the Algemeiner, it was named “Kochav Meir” after Golda Meir.
According to an article in a scientific journal, the war that broke out in Ukraine on February 24, 2022 created a humanitarian crisis with thousands injured and 12 million displaced.
According to the article, the hospital was set up in the town of Mostyska, on the main refugee route, and began operating on March 22, 2022.
According to the Ministry of Health of Ukraine, the staff was made up of Israeli specialists, and care was provided free of charge to anyone who needed it.
According to the article, in six weeks of operation 6,161 patients were treated there, 954 of them children.

stations.title: Before: war, and a damaged medical system

paragraphs.text: On February 24, 2022, hostilities broke out in Ukraine.
According to an article in a scientific journal, a full-scale humanitarian crisis developed, with thousands of civilians injured and 12 million displaced.
According to the article, the crisis led to a severe disruption of routine medical services.
Most elective activity was halted, and residents and refugees were left without basic care.

According to the World Health Organization, from the start of the war until March 13, 31 attacks on health care were documented in Ukraine; in 24 of them health facilities were damaged or destroyed, and in five ambulances were hit.

stations.title: The decision: a civilian hospital, inside Ukraine

paragraphs.text: According to the article's authors, Israel decided for the first time to deploy a civilian field hospital.
According to JNS, the hospital was operated by the Health Ministry, Sheba, Clalit and staff from other hospitals, and not by the IDF Medical Corps as in previous missions.
According to JNS, in 2010 Israel set up a field hospital in Haiti after the earthquake.
According to the article, setting up the hospital in Poland, near the large refugee camps, was initially considered.
But it turned out that most refugees stayed there for only two to three days, and those who needed treatment were treated in Polish hospitals.
According to the Algemeiner, the Israeli government approved the deployment, and Mashav, the Foreign Ministry's aid agency founded by Golda Meir, led the project.
According to Israel Hayom, the hospital was funded by the Israeli government, the Schusterman Foundation and the Joint Distribution Committee.
According to the Algemeiner, Prime Minister Bennett informed President Putin about the hospital in a phone call.
According to a Walla News report that cited two unnamed senior Israeli officials, Israel coordinated the deployment with Russia.

stations.title: Setting up: a school in the town of Mostyska

paragraphs.text: According to the article, the hospital was set up in the town of Mostyska, on the main refugee route, in an area not directly affected by the combat.
According to Israel Hayom, it was set up on the grounds of an elementary school.
According to the article, there was also a tented facility for out-patient activities.
According to the Algemeiner, Israel airlifted 17 tons of equipment to set up the hospital.
According to Euronews, it had 66 beds and was to operate 24 hours a day, seven days a week.
According to the Algemeiner, its capacity was 150 patients.
According to the article, the hospital was completely digital and connected to the IT system of Sheba Medical Center.
According to Israel21c, the Russians asked that the tents be marked so that pilots would recognize a medical facility, but the team brought its own security.
According to Kan News, the hospital had a procedure and drills for evacuation by buses waiting near the gate.

stations.title: The opening: flags, anthems and a name

paragraphs.text: According to JNS, a day before the opening the delegation was sent off in a ceremony attended by Prime Minister Naftali Bennett and Foreign Minister Yair Lapid.
According to the Algemeiner, the hospital opened in Mostyska in a ceremony in which the flags of Israel and Ukraine were raised and the anthems were played.
The hospital was named "Kochav Meir" after Golda Meir, former Prime Minister of Israel, who was born in Ukraine.
According to Israel21c, in 1943 most of the 4,000 Jews who lived in Mostyska before World War II were murdered by the Nazis and Ukrainian collaborators.
Yoel Har-Even of Sheba, the hospital's director, said at the ceremony that the mission connects 1,000 years of Jewish life in the place with today's State of Israel.
He said there is a clear moral obligation not to look away, as human beings, as medical professionals and as Jews.
According to Sheba, 50 patients were treated on the opening day, and three of them were hospitalized.
According to Dr. Har-Even, 40 patients came to the hospital on the first day, 160 on the second day, and 170 patients on Shabbat, from eight in the morning until eight in the evening.
According to Israel Hayom, not many Ukrainians were expected in the first days, because the town is small and remote.

stations.title: The staff: who came to work there

paragraphs.text: According to Israel Hayom, the staff came from various hospitals and health funds and from Magen David Adom, and many of them spoke Russian and Ukrainian.
According to CBN, the hospital was operated by Sheba and Schneider, in cooperation with the Health and Foreign Ministries.
According to Israel21c, the staff included Jews, Muslims and Christians.
According to CBN, many of the staff had Ukrainian roots connected to the Holocaust.
Prof. Elhanan Bar-On said his mother fled at age 15 after her family was murdered in Belzec.
He said he represents the State of Israel and helps anyone in need, friend or foe.
According to CBN, Yoel Har-Even said this is Israel's first civilian field hospital.
According to Israel21c, the hospital received a second shift of volunteers.

stations.title: What actually happened: fewer war wounds, more everyday medicine

paragraphs.text: According to the article, contrary to expectations, the main need was primary care for refugees and residents, because the local medical system had been damaged.
The emphasis shifted from surgery of war wounds to routine ambulatory medicine, and the number of primary care physicians on the team was increased.
According to Dr. Eran Mashiach of Schneider, very few war wounded arrived, and their injuries were not fresh.
According to Israel21c, in the first five days more than 730 locals and refugees were treated and 16,000 lab tests were performed, mainly for problems not related to the war.
According to the Algemeiner, one of the first patients operated on was a 12-year-old girl who fled with her mother.
Dr. Mashiach described a caesarean section at a nearby local hospital with outdated conditions and equipment, in which an Israeli team joined the local team.

According to him, after the baby was born by caesarean section, just as they came to place him on the father, they saw that he was turning very blue and limp, and an Israeli and local team resuscitated him until he recovered and began to cry, in a process that took two to three minutes.

Dr. Mashiach also told of a girl who arrived with a joint disease in her leg and with an earlier diagnosis according to which she would probably have to undergo an amputation. After consulting a hematologist from Schneider, the team understood that a single injection into the knee joint could solve the problem for good.
According to the abstract of a scientific article, telemedicine allowed consultation with the most experienced specialists in Israel.
According to Prof. Bar-On, the hospital's lab is unprecedented in the history of field hospitals in the world.
According to Kan News, a Ukrainian soldier in uniform also came to receive consultation and treatment.
Parents of a ten-year-old girl who fled the Kyiv area thanked the Israeli doctors for the help that helped their daughter get back on her feet.
A woman from the Lviv area told CBN that she has great trust in Israeli medicine, and therefore brought her daughter for a skin examination.
According to Israel21c, a family traveled 48 hours with a girl who underwent surgery in Israel, because it trusts the Israeli healthcare system.

stations.title: The outcome: six weeks, thousands of patients

paragraphs.text: According to Ynet, after about two weeks the delegation had treated about 2,000 patients, about 400 of them children, mainly refugees and local residents.
According to the article, 6,161 patients were treated during the period of operation, 954 of them children.
65 patients were hospitalized, and 59 underwent surgery.
Seven patients were brought to Israel for advanced care that was unavailable in the field hospital or in local facilities.
According to the article, 796 Ukrainian medical personnel received training in medical and psychosocial fields.

According to the article, the hospital was dismantled after six weeks, because the refugee flow declined, there was a sense that the needs of the acute phase had been addressed, and also for budgetary reasons.
Dr. Dudu Dagan, head of the delegation, said there was full cooperation on the part of the local authorities.
According to Dr. Mashiach, the local staff welcomed the Israelis warmly, and the mayor came to eat with them almost every day.
The article's authors wrote that throughout the mission they felt trust and gratitude from the patients, the medical staff and the administrators.

stations.title: Recognition: a ceremony in Jerusalem and a delegation from Lviv

paragraphs.text: Foreign Minister Yair Lapid said at a recognition ceremony that Israel was and remains the only country to send an entire hospital to Ukraine.
He said it was a fully digital hospital, with telemedicine and the ability to continue treatment in a shelter during a siren.
Health Minister Nitzan Horowitz described the hospital as the “pinnacle” of Israeli diplomacy.
Lapid announced that in two weeks a Ukrainian medical delegation from Lviv would arrive in Israel for training in emergency medicine.

claims.text: לפי CBN, ישראל שלחה 10 טון תרופות, מיטות וציוד ויותר מ-60 עובדים, ורבים מהם בעלי שורשים אוקראיניים הקשורים לשואה.
claims.quote: Israel sent 10 tons of medicine plus beds, equipment and more than 60 workers.

claims.text: פרופ' אלחנן בר-און אמר שאמו ברחה בגיל 15 אחרי שמשפחתה נרצחה בבלזץ, ושהוא מייצג את מדינת ישראל ועוזר לכל נזקק, ידיד או אויב.
claims.quote: lending a helping hand, to anyone in need friend or foe and sharing our knowledge with our Ukrainian colleagues because medicine has no boundaries,

claims.text: לפי CBN, יואל הר-אבן אמר שזה בית החולים השדה האזרחי הראשון של ישראל.
claims.quote: Har-Even says while Israel often sponsors medical missions to disaster areas, this is the first civilian field hospital.

claims.text: לפי ישראל21c, בית החולים, שמופעל על ידי שיבא, משרד הבריאות וכללית, טיפל בסמוך ל-2,200 מטופלים וקיבל משמרת מתנדבים שנייה.
claims.quote: has treated nearly 2,200 patients. It’s also received a second shift of volunteers.

claims.text: לפי המאמר, בניגוד לציפיות, הצורך העיקרי היה טיפול ראשוני בפליטים ובתושבים בשל מערכת רפואית שנפגעה.
claims.quote: the main necessity encountered was delivery of primary care to both the refugee and local population, due to the compromised medical system.

claims.text: לפי המאמר, הדגש עבר מניתוחי פצעי מלחמה לרפואה אמבולטורית שגרתית, ומספר רופאי הקהילה בצוות הוגדל.
claims.quote: shifting the emphasis from surgery of war wounds to ambulatory routine medicine, increasing the number of primary care physicians in the team

claims.text: לפי ד"ר משיח, הגיעו מעט מאוד פצועי מלחמה, ופציעותיהם לא היו טריות.
claims.quote: הגיעו מעט מאוד פצועים מהמלחמה, וגם הם עם פציעות לא טריות, שכבר טופלו ודרשו תיקון או חוות דעת שנייה

claims.text: לפי ישראל21c, בחמשת הימים הראשונים טופלו יותר מ-730 מקומיים ופליטים ובוצעו 16,000 בדיקות מעבדה, בעיקר בעיות שאינן קשורות למלחמה.
claims.quote: Within the first five days, the hospital treated more than 730 locals and refugees from other parts of Ukraine and performed 16,000 lab tests.

claims.text: לפי Algemeiner, אחד המטופלים הראשונים שנותחו היה ילדה בת 12 שנמלטה עם אמה.
claims.quote: One of the first patients operated on by Sheba Medical Center staff was a 12-year-old girl who fled with her mother

claims.text: לפי ד"ר משיח, הניתוח נערך בבית חולים מקומי סמוך שתנאיו וציודו מיושנים, וצוות ישראלי הצטרף לצוות המקומי בניתוח.
claims.quote: זה בית חולים מיושן, עם תנאים לא תנאים וציוד מאוד מיושן – משהו שלא מוכר לנו בארץ, אולי משנות החמישים.

claims.text: ד"ר ערן משיח משניידר סיפר שהתינוק שנולד בניתוח קיסרי הפך כחול ורפוי, וצוות ישראלי ומקומי החיה אותו תוך שתיים-שלוש דקות.
claims.quote: זה לקח שתיים-שלוש דקות של עצירת נשימה של כל הנוכחים בחדר, האבא, אנחנו, עד שהתינוק התאושש והתחיל לבכות

claims.text: לפי ד"ר משיח, ילדה עם מחלת פרקים ברגל, שאובחנה כנדרשת לכריתה, טופלה בזריקה אחת למפרק הברך אחרי התייעצות עם המטולוג משניידר.
claims.quote: ואחרי שהתייעצנו עם המטולוג שלנו משניידר הבנו שזריקה אחת למפרק הברך יכולה לפתור את הבעיה לתמיד

claims.text: לפי תקציר המאמר, השימוש ברפואה מרחוק אפשר גישה להתייעצות עם המומחים המנוסים ביותר בישראל.
claims.quote: The use of telemedicine enhanced capabilities, allowing access to consultation with the most experienced specialists in Israel.

claims.text: לפי פרופ' אלחנן בר-און, המעבדה בבית החולים חסרת תקדים בתולדות בתי החולים השדה בעולם.
claims.quote: The lab we have here is unprecedented in the history of field hospitals in the world.

claims.text: לפי כאן חדשות, חיילת אוקראינית במדים הגיעה לקבל ייעוץ וטיפול בבית החולים.
claims.quote: הופתענו לראות כאן חיילת אוקראינית במדים, מתאוששת ממחלה קשה, שבאה לקבל ייעוץ וטיפול ומבקשת שלא להזדהות.

claims.text: הורי ילדה בת עשר שברחה מאזור קייב הודו לרופאים הישראלים על הסיוע שעזר לבתם לקום על הרגליים.
claims.quote: אנחנו רוצים להודות לכל הרופאים מישראל על הסיוע והטיפול הרפואי, שעזרו לבתנו הקטנה לקום על הרגליים

claims.text: אישה מאזור לבוב אמרה ל-CBN שהיא סומכת מאוד על הרפואה הישראלית ולכן הביאה את בתה לבדיקת עור.
claims.quote: As I know there is here an Israel hospital and I have very high trust that Israel medicine.

claims.text: לפי ישראל21c, משפחה נסעה 48 שעות עם ילדה שעברה ניתוח בישראל, כי הם סומכים על מערכת הבריאות הישראלית.
claims.quote: they drove her 48 hours to see us because they trust the Israeli medical system.

claims.text: לפי ynet, אחרי כשבועיים טיפלה המשלחת בכ-2,000 מטופלים, מהם כ-400 ילדים, בעיקר פליטים ותושבי הסביבה.
claims.quote: המשלחת הישראלית טיפלה בכ-2,000 מטופלים עד כה, מתוכם כ-400 ילדים

claims.text: לפי המאמר, 65 מטופלים אושפזו ו-59 עברו ניתוח.
claims.quote: 65 patients were hospitalized and 59 patients underwent surgery.

claims.text: לפי המאמר, שבעה מטופלים הובאו לישראל לטיפול מתוחכם שלא היה זמין בבית החולים השדה או במתקנים המקומיים.
claims.quote: Seven patients were brought to Israel for sophisticated care which was unavailable in the field hospital or in local health facilities.

claims.text: לפי המאמר, בית החולים פורק לאחר שישה שבועות בשל ירידה בזרם הפליטים, התחושה שצורכי השלב החריף נענו, ושיקולי תקציב.
claims.quote: The hospital was dismantled after six weeks of operation as there was a decline in the refugee flow and it was felt that the acute phase needs had been addressed, as well as for budgetary reasons.

claims.text: ד"ר דודו דגן, ראש המשלחת, אמר שהייתה שיתוף פעולה מלא מצד הרשויות המקומיות.
claims.quote: We've had full and appreciable cooperation on the part of local authorities, and we truly believe our hospital will provide a glimmer of hope.

claims.text: לפי ד"ר משיח, הצוות המקומי קיבל את הישראלים בחום, וראשת העיר הגיעה לאכול איתם כמעט כל יום.
claims.quote: קבלת הפנים כאן מדהימה ומרגשת, לא רק ברמה הפוליטית, של ראשת העיר שבאה לאכול איתנו כמעט כל יום

claims.text: לפי מחברי המאמר, לאורך המשימה הם חשו אמון והכרת תודה מצד המטופלים, הצוות הרפואי והמנהלים.
claims.quote: Throughout the mission, we felt a sense of trust and gratitude from all those we encountered – patients, medical staff and administrators.

claims.text: שר החוץ לפיד אמר בטקס הוקרה שישראל הייתה ונשארה המדינה היחידה ששלחה בית חולים שלם לאוקראינה.
claims.quote: Israel was and remains the only country to send an entire hospital into Ukraine,

claims.text: לפיד אמר שזה היה בית חולים בסטנדרט הגבוה בעולם, דיגיטלי לחלוטין, עם רפואה מרחוק ויכולת להמשיך לטפל גם במקלט בזמן אזעקה.
claims.quote: A fully digital hospital, with advanced telemedicine capabilities, and with the ability to go down into a shelter during an air raid siren

claims.text: שר הבריאות ניצן הורוביץ תיאר את בית החולים כ"שיא" של הדיפלומטיה הישראלית.
claims.quote: Horowitz described the field hospital as the “pinnacle” of Israeli diplomacy

claims.text: לפיד הודיע שבעוד שבועיים תגיע לישראל משלחת רפואית אוקראינית מלבוב להכשרה ברפואת חירום.
claims.quote: Lapid announced Sunday that in two weeks, a Ukrainian medical delegation from Lviv is expected to arrive in Israel to receive training in emergency medicine.

claims.text: לפי ynet, 17 טון ציוד הוטסו לאוקראינה להקמת בית החולים.
claims.quote: הוטסו לאוקראינה 17 טון של ציוד להקמת בית החולים

claims.text: לפי ישראל היום, צוות של 80 איש יפעיל את בית החולים, שמתוכנן לפעול לפחות חודש.
claims.quote: will be operated by a team of 80 people. The plan is for the hospital to operate for at least a month

claims.text: לפי ישראל21c, בבית החולים 66 מיטות ונמצאים בו 70 מתנדבים ישראלים, ולדברי הר-אבן הוא מנהל אותו.
claims.quote: the 70 Israeli volunteers staffing the field hospital were already safe inside the building

claims.text: לפי Algemeiner, אחרי שישה שבועות טיפלו כ-210 אנשי צוות בלמעלה מ-6,000 פליטים אוקראינים, ביניהם 750 ילדים, בבית החולים בן 66 המיטות.
claims.quote: Some 210 staff treated more than 6,000 Ukrainian refugees, including 750 children, at the 66-bed center

claims.text: לפי משרד הבריאות של אוקראינה, כל צוות רופאים עתיד לעבוד במשמרת של שבוע.
claims.quote: Each team of doctors will work in shift for a week.

claims.text: לפי יהודה קטורזה מצוות הלוגיסטיקה של שיבא, צוות של 80 אנשי רפואה יגיע, והצוותים יוחלפו כל שבועיים.
claims.quote: will consist of 80 medical staff that will cross into Ukraine and begin work as early as Tuesday.

claims.text: לפי ynet, "כוכב מאיר" הוא בית חולים השדה הרשמי היחיד בכל אוקראינה, ולדברי ד"ר משיח ארגון אמריקאי בלבוב מטפל בהרבה פחות מטופלים.
claims.quote: יש בלבוב עוד בית חולים של ארגון אמריקאי, לא משהו רשמי, והבנו שהם רואים הרבה פחות מטופלים מאיתנו

claims.text: לפי Euronews, ישראל היא המדינה הראשונה שהקימה בית חולים שדה באוקראינה.
claims.quote: Israel is the first country to establish a field hospital in Ukraine.

quote_translations.c49: that Israel set up in the town of Mostyska (Mostyska) in western Ukraine, at a distance of about 12 kilometers from the border with Poland.
quote_translations.c83: In a field hospital there is a procedure and drills for evacuation and escape by means of buses that wait here all the time near the gate.
quote_translations.c53: Very few wounded from the war arrived, and they too with injuries that were not fresh, that had already been treated and required correction or a second opinion
quote_translations.c51: It is an outdated hospital, with conditions that are not conditions and very outdated equipment – something we are not familiar with in Israel, maybe from the fifties.
quote_translations.c50: It took two to three minutes of everyone present in the room holding their breath, the father, us, until the baby recovered and began to cry
quote_translations.c54: And after we consulted with our hematologist from Schneider we understood that a single injection into the knee joint could solve the problem for good
quote_translations.c82: We were surprised to see here a Ukrainian soldier in uniform, recovering from a serious illness, who came to receive consultation and treatment and asks not to be identified.
quote_translations.c84: We want to thank all the doctors from Israel for the assistance and the medical treatment, which helped our little daughter get back on her feet
quote_translations.c52: The Israeli delegation has treated about 2,000 patients so far, of them about 400 children
quote_translations.c57: The welcome here is amazing and moving, not only at the political level, of the mayor who comes to eat with us almost every day
quote_translations.c56: 17 tons of equipment were flown to Ukraine to set up the hospital
quote_translations.c55: In Lviv there is another hospital of an American organization, not something official, and we understood that they see far fewer patients than us
